title: Knuckle rush, raze gameplay
author: Darkonxy
selftext: Hey guys! I wanted to show you the game I’m developing. Most of the graphics were created using AI and then refined/edited by hand. Any feedback is welcome (except for "you just did this with a couple of prompts on Claude" :D)

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
Sprites look clean and the animations are fuid; I like the overall presentation. That install special move needs some work but I like the camera zoom. 

What tool(s) did you use for the sprites and/or the animation?

replies.author: Darkonxy
replies.body: hi! i used pixellab AI, it's very powerful but you need to fix alot ;)

comments.author: The-Dire-Llama
comments.body: love it, the streets of rage vibe is bringing back memories!

comments.author: moschles
comments.body: You have the enemies blink and disappear?  What is this, an 8bit console?   Have the dead enemies  lay there and turn grey or something.

replies.author: Darkonxy
replies.body: Well, the resolution is 420x240,so, not 8-bit, but definitely 16-bit! :D Jokes aside, your idea is cool and wouldn't even be that hard to implement. The only issue is that, as you can see, the enemies reappear in every wave; it would look pretty strange to see the same enemy lying dead on the ground while you're trying to fight! :D

comments.author: Material_Run_5570
comments.body:
Cool. I always liked this genre.   
I have no clue about ai gamedev so I'm curious If I would be able to create a game like that.

What were the biggest challenges and what sucked the most time?

replies.author: Darkonxy
replies.body: Hi! Definitely the graphic design side of things. While AI tools are a huge help, achieving a convincing result still requires a significant amount of human input. As for the code—well, I’ve been a programmer for 20 years, and using AI coding agents certainly sped up the process (though I still spent a lot of time refining things to reach a result that was, at least to me, satisfying and well-balanced).
